name: SGMRI-VQA
description: SGMRI-VQA (Spatially Grounded MRI Visual Question Answering) is a multi-frame, spatially grounded VQA benchmark for brain and knee MRI. It comprises 41,307 QA pairs derived from 1,866 unique MRI volumes (892 brain + 974 knee), each paired with a clinician-aligned chain-of-thought reasoning trace and frame-indexed bounding-box coordinates. Tasks are organized hierarchically across detection, localization, classification, counting, and captioning. The benchmark provides two evaluation granularities: image-level (single-slice, five tasks: detection, localization, classification, diagnosis, captioning) and multi-frame (entire scan as a sequence, five tasks: detection, localization, counting, classification, captioning). QA pairs were generated by GPT-4o under clinician-built prompt templates that integrate fastMRI+ expert metadata (per-slice radiologist bounding boxes, finding labels, scan-level diagnoses) as ground-truth context, then curated through a deterministic metadata-anchored cleaning pipeline and reviewed by a board-certified clinician with 20+ years in clinical practice and brain/knee subspecialty training.

rai:dataLimitations: Single-institution source: all scans originate from a single tertiary care center, likely containing biases related to regional healthcare practices, scanner vendors, and acquisition protocols. Limited domain coverage: only brain and knee MRI; not validated for other anatomical regions, modalities, or imaging protocols. Pathology range: limited to the finding categories available in fastMRI+ (9 brain, 22 knee categories); rare or institution-specific pathologies are not represented. The benchmark is intended for research only and is explicitly not recommended for direct clinical decision-making, autonomous diagnostic deployment, or clinical interpretation without expert oversight.
rai:dataBiases: Demographic skew: patient demographics reflect the source institution's catchment population (single hospital). Scanner bias: all scans acquired on a small set of Siemens Magnetom scanners (Aera 1.5T, Skyra 3T, Prisma 3T, Biograph mMR 3T). Sequence bias: brain scans use only axial FLAIR and T1-weighted sequences; knee scans use only sagittal proton-density-weighted with fat saturation. Selection bias: fastMRI+ images were selected and annotated by the original authors and may not be representative of all clinical cases. Finding-category imbalance: certain categories (e.g., nonspecific white matter lesions for brain, meniscus tear for knee) appear more frequently than others, reflecting clinical prevalence in the source cohort rather than balanced sampling.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains medical imaging data (MRI scans of human patients) sourced from fastMRI+, which is itself derived from de-identified scans. No direct identifiers (PHI) are included. Users are responsible for verifying compliance with HIPAA, GDPR, or equivalent regional health-data regulations for their specific use case. The dataset does not include race, ethnicity, socio-economic status, or other demographic attributes beyond what is implicit in the imaging itself.
rai:dataUseCases: Recommended uses: (i) benchmarking vision-language models on multi-frame spatially grounded medical reasoning, (ii) supervised fine-tuning research on grounded clinical reasoning, (iii) evaluation of chain-of-thought reasoning quality in radiology, (iv) studies of cross-slice visual grounding capabilities. Not recommended: direct clinical decision-making, autonomous diagnosis, training models for unsupervised radiology workflows, or any clinical application without expert oversight. Construct validity: the dataset measures VLM ability to localize and reason about MRI findings using radiologist-annotated bounding boxes as the ground truth; it does not measure broader clinical reasoning beyond the annotated finding categories.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive impact: advances grounded medical AI research, supports development of explainable VLMs for radiology with transparent spatial reasoning, provides a standardized benchmark that enables reproducible comparison across the medical-VLM community. Risks: misuse for unsupervised clinical decisions; over-reliance on AI-generated reasoning traces; misinterpretation of benchmark performance as clinical readiness; potential reinforcement of biases inherited from a single-institution source. Mitigations: explicit not-for-clinical-use labeling; comprehensive limitations documentation in both dataset card and accompanying paper; release of model outputs alongside ground truth so users can audit failure modes.
prov:wasGeneratedBy: Provenance pipeline: (1) Source data: fastMRI+ provides expert radiologist bounding-box annotations, finding labels, and scan-level diagnoses across brain (axial FLAIR, T1-weighted) and knee (sagittal proton-density-weighted with fat saturation) MRI volumes. (2) Preprocessing: HDF5 volumes converted to per-slice grayscale PNG images with orientation correction and min-max normalization; bounding-box annotations matched to slices by volume identifier and slice index; volumes without valid annotations filtered out. (3) QA generation: GPT-4o was prompted using clinician-built templates that integrate the expert metadata as structured context (modality, scan-level diagnosis, per-slice finding label, bounding-box coordinates with frame indices). The model rephrases this metadata into natural-language QA pairs with chain-of-thought reasoning at two granularities (image-level and multi-frame), across five tasks per granularity. The pipeline is not end-to-end synthetic generation: clinical labels come from radiologist annotations and only descriptive language is generated by GPT-4o. (4) Curation: a four-stage metadata-anchored pipeline corrects systematic GPT-4o errors (primarily laterality assignment) using deterministic rules keyed on the ground-truth bounding boxes (e.g., bounding-box x-coordinate determines brain hemisphere; manually annotated fibula side determines knee medial/lateral). (5) Annotation/review: a board-certified clinician with 20+ years in clinical practice and brain/knee subspecialty training reviewed every test-set sample (100% coverage, 222 brain + 155 knee testing volumes) and verified a stratified random sample of 300 training QA pairs spanning both image-level and multi-frame granularities; approximately 96% of the training-sample reasoning traces were rated correct as-generated. The released test set has all flagged issues corrected during review, serving as the gold-standard benchmark.

distribution.name: huggingface-repo
distribution.description: Hugging Face dataset repository containing all SGMRI-VQA files.

distribution.name: qa-pairs
distribution.description: JSON files containing brain and knee MRI question-answer pairs with chain-of-thought reasoning traces and ground-truth bounding-box coordinates. Files are organized in brain/ and knee/ subfolders and follow the naming pattern gpt4o_{domain}_{train,test,val}_{image,volume}_qa_*_qa_pairs.json.

distribution.name: brain-train-images
distribution.description: TAR archive of brain MRI training images (per-slice grayscale PNGs).

distribution.name: brain-test-images
distribution.description: TAR archive of brain MRI test images (per-slice grayscale PNGs).

distribution.name: knee-train-images
distribution.description: TAR archive of knee MRI training images (per-slice grayscale PNGs).

distribution.name: knee-test-images
distribution.description: TAR archive of knee MRI test images (per-slice grayscale PNGs).

distribution.name: brain-images
distribution.description: Per-slice brain MRI grayscale PNG images extracted from the brain TAR archives.

distribution.name: knee-images
distribution.description: Per-slice knee MRI grayscale PNG images extracted from the knee TAR archives.

recordSet.name: qa-records
recordSet.description: Each record is a single question-answer pair derived from one MRI sample (slice or scan).

field.name: volume_id
field.description: Unique identifier of the source MRI volume in fastMRI+.

field.name: slice_num
field.description: Frame index of the slice within the volume (image-level QA pairs only; absent for multi-frame).

field.name: modality
field.description: MRI sequence (e.g., FLAIR, T1, T2, PD-FS).

field.name: type
field.description: Question format: open_ended, closed_ended, single_choice, or multiple_choice.

field.name: task
field.description: Task category: detection, localization, classification, diagnosis, counting, or captioning.

field.name: answer
field.description: Reference answer; for localization tasks, includes inline <bbx>[x,y,w,h]</bbx> coordinates with frame indices.

field.name: reasoning
field.description: Clinician-aligned chain-of-thought reasoning trace explaining how the answer is derived from the visual evidence.

field.name: ground_truth
field.description: Structured ground truth: bounding-box coordinates {x, y, width, height, label} (pixel space) and finding/diagnosis labels.
